messages:
Maria: Heads-up: bringing Seraphon-7B into our int4 pipeline. Quick smoke shows long-context QA collapse after conversion. Suspect rotary head interleave + vocab base mishandle. Posting quick numbers and snippets.

Maria: LongQA-smoke (1k): fp16 baseline F1=0.77 EM=0.63; after int4+rotary-conv F1=0.46 EM=0.29. Dev PPX ~12 -> ~20 after convert.

Alex: ouch. Which converter flags + tokenmap did you use? Rotary params sourced from checkpoint or inferred?

Maria: command: `tools/convert_seraphon.py --ckpt seraphon/7b.pt --out seraphon-7b.onnx --rotary head-concat --quant int4 --vocab-map seraphon->unified.json`

Maria: tokenmap (excerpt): `{"token_offset":2,"eos":50256}`

Kai: my bet is head interleaving. Some exporters store heads interleaved and a reshape without a proper transpose will mix head angles. That kills long-range attention.

Alex: can you dump rotary angle arrays for first few heads from both ckpt and converted artifact? Use `python -c "from tools.dump import dump_rotary; dump_rotary('seraphon/7b.pt',0,6)"` and same for the onnx.

Maria: pasted truncated arrays:
orig head0: [0.000,0.017,0.034,0.051,...]
conv head0: [0.000,0.034,0.068,0.102,...]
conv head1 matches orig head2 pattern. Looks like stride doubled + head permutation.

Kai: that matches an exporter flattening [feature,head] vs [head,feature] then reshape issue. Two fixes: detect & correct head permutation via correlation; detect any frequency/stride scaling (maybe a unit mismatch during serialization/quant).

Alex: propose patch in converter: after loading angles do `angles = angles.reshape(n_heads, -1)` then compute `perm = np.argmax(np.abs(angles @ orig_angles.T), axis=1)` and reorder. Also check median ratio between matched vectors to detect scale factor and correct if ratio~2. Guard the auto-fix with a threshold.

Maria: applied patch locally (head perm detect + scale correction) and re-ran int4 pipeline. New smoke: F1=0.65 EM=0.50 PPX~13.2. Much better but still behind. Remaining delta likely quantization of embeddings / final projection or LN folding.

Kai: next step: run conversions in bf16 and int8 to isolate pure quant noise. Also compute embedding similarity: sample 10k tokens, compute cosine/dot between ckpt embeddings and converted embeddings. If L2 err > 1e-2 suspect projection truncation or accidental transpose.

Alex: double-check token offset handling. Your tokenmap had token_offset:2; did converter subtract once or twice? Off-by-one in BOS/EOS can show up as weird long-context degradation.

Maria: double-checked metadata: checkpoint `vocab_base=2`. Converter subtracts base, but I found codepath that applied an extra subtraction when building special-token remap. Token sanity test: sample "Hello" maps orig [154,42,7] conv [152,40,5] -> shifted by 2. Fixing single subtraction brought token ids back to original.

Maria: with head-perm+scale fix + token-offset fix: F1=0.70 EM=0.57 PPX~12.6. Remaining gap ~0.06 F1.

Kai: run ablation: quantize only transformer body, keep embeddings & final linear in fp16. If score recovers, we add allowlist.

Maria: ablation (embeds+proj fp16, body int4) -> F1=0.73 EM=0.61. Pretty close to fp16 baseline.

Alex: plan: add `--fp16-proj` flag to converter to allow layer-level fp16 preserve and make `--head-perm-detect` enabled by default. I'll push change to branch `alex/seraphon-rotary-fix` and run canary.

ci-bot: pipeline queued: service=converter, branch=alex/seraphon-rotary-fix, environment=dedicated-seraphon-canary, ETA~6m :rocket:

Kai: also add unit test `tools/tests/test_rotary_headperm.py` that synthesizes interleaved head tensor and asserts detection recovers ordering and scale. Add a small embedding stability test too.

Maria: filing issue with logs, diffs, and experiment results. Will attach dumps and eval config.

Alex: once canary pass, we'll update int4 recipes for Seraphon family to use `--fp16-proj` and publish release notes mentioning head-perm auto-detect. I'll draft RFC to generalize detection across converters.

Maria: thanks all. Closing this thread after issue/PR links in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
